veranderings.na: wat diere agter hulle aan trek
veranderings.rede: The circumposition is 'agter ... aan' plus 'trek'; written together, 'aantrek' means to dress or to attract.

veranderings.voor: trek 'n vrag baie swaarder as die karretjie s'n
veranderings.na: trek 'n baie swaarder vrag as die karretjie s'n
veranderings.rede: The comparative goes before the noun in natural Afrikaans; same words, same meaning.
'Saamgeneem' is the standard written form; 'saamgevat' is colloquial.

veranderings.voor: wat perde of muile getrek het
veranderings.na: wat deur perde of muile getrek is
veranderings.rede: As written, 'wat' can be read as the subject, so the coach pulls the horses; the passive removes the ambiguity for one extra word.
'Vervoer' is the natural verb for a vehicle carrying passengers; 'mense gedra' sounds like carrying them in your arms.
'Op een slag' is the idiomatic Afrikaans expression; same word count.

veranderings.voor: Die voertuig was nuut en die dier
veranderings.na: Die voertuig was nuut, maar die dier
veranderings.rede: Two clauses each with their own subject and verb take a comma (AWS 2017), and 'maar' makes the intended contrast between new and unchanged explicit.

veranderings.voor: Die pedale draai die ketting en die ketting
veranderings.na: Die pedale draai die ketting, en die ketting
veranderings.rede: Both joined clauses have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en'.

veranderings.blok: Geen dier om te voer nie
veranderings.rede: Both joined clauses have their own subject and verb ('hy staan', 'niemand hoef'), so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en'.

veranderings.blok: Vroeë fietse en fietse van vandag
veranderings.rede: 'Reguit' means straight (in direction); 'direk' says the pedals were fixed straight onto the wheel, which is the meaning here.

veranderings.voor: perde of muile trek, en waarin
veranderings.na: perde of muile trek en waarin
veranderings.rede: 'En waarin' joins two relative clauses within one sentence, not two sentences with their own subjects, so AWS 2017 takes no comma.

vlae.teks: 'n Klein voertuig met twee wiele wat diere trek ... / 'n Groot voertuig met vier wiele wat diere trek ... / 'n Voertuig met twee wiele wat die ryer met pedale aandryf.
vlae.rede: In each definition 'wat' can be read as the subject and attaches next to 'wiele', so a literal reading says the wheels pull the animals or drive the rider. A passive form ('wat deur diere getrek word', 'wat die ryer met pedale aandryf' recast) would fix it but adds words near the ceiling and touches definitions that may be shared, so this is left for the reviewer or writer to decide.
